# Code Copilot Team

> An enforceable harness for AI-assisted coding: your rules, your workflow and your safety rails, applied the same way by every coding agent you use.

Experimental: llms.txt is a proposal (llmstxt.org), not a standard. This file is generated by scripts/generate-llms-txt.sh from the same registry as the documentation index, and links to the Markdown on the `master` branch, which is ahead of the latest release.

## Start here

- [Documentation — all of it, grouped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/README.md): Everything written down about Code Copilot Team, grouped the way the Studio's **Learn** tab groups it — this page and that tab read the same registry, so they cannot disagree about what exists
- [Code Copilot Team — README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/README.md): An enforceable harness for AI-assisted coding: your rules, your workflow and your safety rails, applied the same way by every coding agent you use
- [Developer Cookbook — the SDLC of this project](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/developer-cookbook.md): How a change moves from idea to merged PR in **code-copilot-team**, in two modes:
- [Auto code review — setup cookbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/auto-code-review-setup.md): How to have a second model review your work automatically: which reviewer, what goes in the provider profile, how to prove it works before it gates a run, how to turn it on per session and per unattended build, and where to read the result
- [Feature Index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/features.md): generated from its sources; edit the source, not the page
- [Feature maturity, release state and adapter support](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/maturity.md): The feature catalog (`shared/features/catalog.yaml`) records four separate things about every user-facing feature
- [Shape-Up Workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/shape-up-workflow.md): Shape-Up is Basecamp's product development methodology
- [Spec-Driven Development vs Code Copilot Team](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/sdd-vs-code-copilot-team.md): A side-by-side comparison of two complementary approaches to AI-assisted software development

## Feature guides

- [Spec-Driven Development (SDD)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/spec-driven-development.md): The specification, plan and task artifacts a feature needs before code is written, the gates that enforce them, and what each adapter can do about it
- [Peer Review (Multi-Copilot)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/peer-review.md): How a second model reviews your work: the round, the verdict contract, the findings file, the fallback chain, and every switch that turns it on
- [Unattended auto-build](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/auto-build.md): The driver that builds an approved feature phase by phase outside a session, and the four gates that decide whether a phase lands: the caps that stop a run, the coverage contract, the runtime conformance evaluator, and the visual verification gate
- [LLM Routing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/llm-routing.md): Routing an auto-build task to a backend by route class and role, under an execution profile
- [Project Templates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/project-templates.md): The eleven stack templates, what each one's agent team looks like, and the CI workflow each ships
- [Configuration Reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/configuration-reference.md): generated from its sources; edit the source, not the page
- [Repo Structure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/repo-structure.md): Where everything lives in this repository, for contributors
- [Configuration Layers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/configuration-layers.md): Where each rule, skill, agent and hook is installed, and which layer wins when two of them say different things. **More specific always wins:** a project's `CLAUDE.md` overrides the global manifest, and `CLAUDE.local.md` overrides both
- [Install Options](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/install.md): Every install path, for every tool

## Analytics & benchmarks

- [Session Analytics — user cookbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/session-analytics-cookbook.md): Session Analytics reads the transcripts your AI coding assistant leaves on disk (Claude Code, Aider, Pi), stores them in a local database, and opens a Studio where you can see what happened in your sessions, find what to fix in your harness, and measure whether the numbers can be trusted
- [Session Analytics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/scripts/session_analytics/README.md): Copilot session analytics & process-mining pipeline (issue #63) — the **Claude Code analyzer**, mirroring the architecture of the upstream kiro-analyzer (which already covers Kiro)
- [Benchmark Harness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/benchmarks/README.md): Benchmark-agnostic runner for evaluating AI copilots and LLMs on coding tasks under reproducible isolation, with deterministic scoring and SDD-aware run records
- [Knowledge Layer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/knowledge/README.md): A durable, structured knowledge layer for `code-copilot-team`, designed to be read and maintained by both humans and AI agents, and to outlive any single session
- [CCT Capability Compatibility Matrix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/shared/capabilities/COMPATIBILITY.md): generated from its sources; edit the source, not the page

## Judge on a DGX Spark

- [DGX Spark — setup & cookbook (Ollama, vLLM, Open WebUI)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/dgx-spark/setup-cookbook.md): **Revision 2 — 2026-09-07.** Changes from revision 1 are listed in *What changed and why* at the end
- [DGX Spark + vLLM — Qwen3.8-27B operator manual](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/dgx-spark/vllm-qwen38.md): **Revised 2026-08-28.** Two different things are being tracked here, and conflating them is the main way to misread this document. **The model is verified on this hardware class.** A published run on a single GB10 with 121.63 GiB usable brought up `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` on vLLM `0.26.1rc1` at the native 262,144-token window, with no vLLM modifications, and exercised reasoning, tool calling, MTP speculative decoding, long context and memory. vLLM has since published an official Qwen3.8-27B recipe (updated 2026-08-26) covering the NVFP4 checkpoint, FP8 KV cache, the Qwen reasoning parser, structured tool calling and MTP
- [DGX Spark — Qwen3.8-27B runbook (exact sequence)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/dgx-spark/runbook-qwen38.md): Two machines

## Background

- [Evidence & Influences](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/evidence-and-influences.md): External reviews, scorecards, and the sources that shaped this harness
- [Case study: an A/B autonomous build of MAP-ATLAS (Claude Code vs pi.dev)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/mapatlas-harness-experiment.md): A hands-off experiment: two AI coding harnesses built the **same** open-source product — **MAP-ATLAS** (repository not yet public), a domain-agnostic TypeScript mapping engine — from an identical, harness-neutral specification, phase by phase, and were scored on a fixed rubric with every claim independently verified
- [GitHub Hardening Playbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gosha70/code-copilot-team/master/docs/github-hardening-playbook.md): This playbook sets repository-level guardrails that complement in-repo checks
